open_points.subject: State 0 acceptance
open_points.text: “State 0 closes again when its question rounds are clear; the owner then accepts it as a whole” and “None open.” No later acceptance or closure is recorded.
open_points.question: Is the reopened State 0 now closed and accepted, or must an explicit owner acceptance still occur before later states may use it?
options: Record explicit acceptance and closure now
Keep State 0 reopened pending owner acceptance
open_points.default_guess: Keep it reopened until the owner explicitly accepts the revised whole.

open_points.subject: Owner sign-in
open_points.text: “Every request on either is authenticated; anything not authenticated is refused” conflicts with “The owner signs in to the owner interface with the owner credential and gets a protected session.”
open_points.question: Which unauthenticated request, if any, is allowed to submit the owner credential, and what observable success and failure does sign-in produce?
options: Allow only the sign-in request before authentication
Authenticate every request directly with the owner credential
Use an authentication system outside Registry
open_points.default_guess: Allow an unauthenticated sign-in submission that returns a protected session or a generic authentication refusal; require that session for every other owner-interface operation.

open_points.subject: Owner discovery of agent sessions and requests
open_points.text: “the owner sees the registered sessions in the owner interface” and “the owner sees [a pending request] in the owner interface,” but no action lists or reads sessions or their pending requests.
open_points.question: What Registry action lets the owner discover registered sessions, inspect their current access and pending request, and what does it return or refuse?
options: Add an owner action listing sessions with access and pending-request state
Include the pending request in the existing per-session access read
Require the owner to know a session id through some named external system
open_points.default_guess: Add an owner-only session list/detail action that exposes each session’s access and pending request without personal data.

open_points.subject: Declined access request outcome
open_points.text: “declining changes nothing; the session reads the outcome in its access,” while “read the session's access” returns only granted project ids, the active project and the access version.
open_points.question: How can the session distinguish a declined request from one that is still pending, and does answering a request clear it and move the access version?
options: Return pending/request outcome in the access read
Clear the request and increment the access version on either grant or decline
Do not expose decline completion to the session
open_points.default_guess: Clear the pending request and increment the access version for either answer, with the access read exposing that no request remains.

open_points.subject: Unknown agent session
open_points.text: “an unknown session answers that it has no access” conflicts with R0-53: “A call naming a session that is not registered is refused like a call outside the set.”
open_points.question: Does reading access for an unknown session return an empty access object or an indistinguishable refusal?
options: Return an indistinguishable refusal
Return an empty access object
open_points.default_guess: Return the same refusal used for an unregistered or unauthorized session.

open_points.subject: Migration closure
open_points.text: The import action says “after the first successful production import the operation is closed and refused,” while R0-54 and R0-59 say “Each source's first successful import into production closes the operation for that source” and permit one VPS import and one test-rig import.
open_points.question: Is migration closed globally after one successful import, or independently after one successful import from each named source?
options: Close independently for VPS and test rig
Close globally after whichever source succeeds first
open_points.default_guess: Close independently per source, allowing one successful VPS import and one successful test-rig import.

open_points.subject: Restriction enforcement
open_points.text: “any operation using its restricted personal data is refused unless the law provides an exception” does not identify the affected operations, the input that asserts an exception, or the actor that decides it; R0-59 also narrows restriction to customer contact data.
open_points.question: Exactly which Registry operations are refused while a customer is restricted, and how does Registry know that a lawful exception applies?
options: Enumerate refused operations and require an owner-supplied exception assertion
Implement no per-operation exception; the owner lifts the restriction when governance permits
Treat restriction only as blocking new project-customer links and non-owner contact disclosure
open_points.default_guess: Block new project-customer links and all non-owner disclosure of contact data; allow the stated owner read, correction and erasure actions, and require the owner to lift the restriction rather than making Registry evaluate legal exceptions.

open_points.subject: Erasing a project with session access
open_points.text: “erase an archived project” may anonymise or delete it, while session grants can retain archived projects and an active project; the text does not say what happens to grants, active selections or later agent projections when the project is erased.
open_points.question: When an archived project is anonymised or deleted, is it removed from every session’s granted set, is an active selection cleared, and what do later session and projection reads return?
options: Remove it from all grants and clear matching active selections for either erasure mode
Keep anonymised projects granted but remove wholly deleted projects
Leave all grants as dangling ids and let project operations answer archived or not found
open_points.default_guess: Remove either erased form from all session grants and clear matching active selections atomically.

open_points.subject: Audit event coverage
open_points.text: Registry records “significant changes of state,” followed by a partial category list, while “Ordinary reads, agent calls and the inner steps of flows are not recorded”; it is unclear whether room, artifact, session registration, active-project, access-request, import and failed-change outcomes are logged.
open_points.question: Which primary actions and which outcomes create audit entries, including state-changing calls made by an agent through Kernel and refused attempts?
options: Enumerate every audited action and outcome explicitly
Audit every successful state-changing primary action
Audit only the categories literally named in R0-58
open_points.default_guess: Audit every successful state-changing primary action, including agent-authority mutations, and do not audit reads or refused attempts unless separately designated as security events.

open_points.subject: Audit-log retention
open_points.text: The audit log “is kept for a limited period the governance documents,” but R0-60 says “Registry erases nothing on its own,” and no owner action removes expired audit entries.
open_points.question: What action or external actor applies the audit-log retention period, and what observable result and failure does that operation have?
options: Add an owner-confirmed audit-pruning action
Let an external administrative process delete expired audit entries outside Registry
Retain audit entries indefinitely
open_points.default_guess: Add an owner-authorized retention-review action that removes audit entries selected under governance and records no erased personal values.

open_points.subject: Customer record deletion
open_points.text: R0-57 says “Until its record is deleted the owner may resume the relationship,” but the only customer erasure action removes contact data and deliberately keeps the Customer identity; no action deletes the Customer record.
open_points.question: Can a Customer record ever be deleted whole, and if so what happens to projects that name its customer_ref, session-visible data and validate/read results?
options: Add whole-customer deletion with defined link effects
Customer stubs are permanent; remove the reference to record deletion
Delete the customer only as part of erasing every linked archived project
open_points.default_guess: Customer stubs remain permanently after contact-data erasure, so the reference to whole-record deletion should be removed.

open_points.subject: onboard_object lifecycle and authority
open_points.text: “The operator script onboard_object: a client of the API like any consumer” remains, but “its staff-credential use ends with R0-30,” the Operator actor was removed, and the owner credential “is held by no tool, agent or service.”
open_points.question: Is onboard_object retired, or what named principal, credential and allowed operations let it remain an API client?
options: Retire it completely
Give it a named service identity and narrowly scoped service token
Let the human owner invoke it using the owner credential
open_points.default_guess: Retire it; its former responsibilities are now carried by the owner interface and Kernel flows.
